title: Quasi-finite finite type ring maps do not increase local dimension
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a finite type homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image. If the map is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}\le\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$, where these are Krull dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Put $T=\{s\in S:\ s\text{ is integral over }R\}$, the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q\cap T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-zariski-main-away], finite type and quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$ give $g\in T\setminus\mathfrak q'$ such that $T_g\to S_g$ is an isomorphism. The prime $\mathfrak qS_g$ corresponds under it to $\mathfrak q'T_g$: a fraction $t/g^n$ with $t\in T$ belongs to $\mathfrak qS_g$ exactly when $t\in\mathfrak q$, because $g\notin\mathfrak q$. Localizing this isomorphism at those primes, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] identifies $S_{\mathfrak q}$ with $T_{\mathfrak q'}$ as rings. Moreover the contraction of $\mathfrak q'$ to $R$ is $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QF (lemma-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite), proof, lines 31281-31285; Theorem Tag 00Q9 (theorem-main-theorem), statement, lines 30778-30788

proof.text: Take any chain $\mathfrak q'_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q'_n\subseteq\mathfrak q'$ of prime ideals of $T$. Since $T$ is integral over $R$ by its definition, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] makes the contractions $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak q'_i\cap R$ a strictly increasing chain of primes of $R$. Each $\mathfrak p_i$ is contained in $\mathfrak q'\cap R=\mathfrak p$, so this is a chain of length $n$ below $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OJ (lemma-integral-dim-up), proof, lines 27348-27356, as invoked by Lemma Tag 00QF, line 31285; incomparability is Lemma Tag 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], the dimension of $T_{\mathfrak q'}$ is the supremum of lengths of chains of primes of $T$ below $\mathfrak q'$, and the dimension of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is the corresponding supremum below $\mathfrak p$. Step 2 sends every chain counted by the first supremum to one of the same length counted by the second. Therefore $\dim T_{\mathfrak q'}\le\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$. The ring isomorphism from step 1 preserves prime chains, so $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\dim T_{\mathfrak q'}$, proving the claim, including infinite-dimensional local rings.
